title: Correctness of the 3-SAT to Clique reduction
statement: Let $f$ be a 3-CNF formula with $m$ clauses. Then $f$ is satisfiable if and only if its conflict graph has a clique of size $m$; that is, the graph whose vertices are the literal positions of $f$, with two positions adjacent exactly when they lie in different clauses and their literals do not conflict, contains $m$ pairwise-adjacent vertices precisely when some truth assignment satisfies every clause of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a 3-CNF formula (a list of 3-clauses)
the clique size sought equals the number of clauses m = f.length
replaced:
A 3-CNF formula $f$ is satisfiable if and only if its conflict graph contains a
clique of size $f.\mathtt{length}$:
\[
  \mathtt{is3Satisfiable}\,f \;\iff\;
  \mathtt{hasClique}\,(\mathtt{toCliqueGraph}\,f)\,f.\mathtt{length}.
\]
